The parser requires the fixed CRW signature in the same attacker-controlled buffer, so a crafted file can satisfy the format gate and reach CIFF directory parsing.
The attacker-chosen headerLength is used to create a substream over the directory region, propagating control of the parse cursor into the directory body.

Each crafted 10-byte directory entry is converted into a CiffEntry object, carrying attacker-controlled tag/type/size metadata into higher-level logic.
The crafted entry uses the inline-data path and an ASCII tag, so the entry's data stream is built directly from attacker bytes rather than validated external offsets.
For CIFF_ASCII, the element shift is zero, so the attacker-chosen byte size becomes the logical string count without additional bounds reduction.
The parser later compares the attacker-supplied make/model string against "Canon", so the crafted ASCII payload is propagated into decoder selection logic.
The ASCII payload is exposed as a C++ string view over the attacker-controlled bytes, preserving the crafted contents for downstream consumers.

The vulnerable sink is the construction of a std::string from attacker-controlled bytes and length; if the crafted CIFF ASCII entry is malformed or unterminated, this path can drive memory-safety failure during string handling and subsequent parsing.
